page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-standard-2 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor using the x86_64 architecture. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to a single physical core with 2 threads per core. The memory configuration consists of 8.0 GB of RAM, providing 4.0 GB per core. This instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, and it comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results show a divergence between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The single-core CPU performance is strong, ranking in the top 25% according to stress-ng. However, multi-core CPU performance is weak, falling into the bottom 25%. Memory performance is generally limited, with read-only large block bandwidth at 26.64 GB/sec and write large block bandwidth at 20.4 GB/sec, both categorized as weak. Passmark memory and database operations scores are poor, placing in the bottom 10%. Single-threaded tasks like gzip compression and bzip3 decompression show average performance.

Given its hardware profile and benchmark results, the n2d-standard-2 is positioned as a cost-efficient option for lightweight general-purpose workloads. It is suitable for basic web serving, text processing, and simple single-threaded applications. It is less suited for memory-intensive databases, multi-threaded compilation, or complex mathematical simulations due to its low multi-core and memory bandwidth scores.
description: The Google Cloud Platform n2d-standard-2 is an x86_64 general-purpose instance configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs and 8.0 GB of RAM, powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor. It features 1 physical core with 2 threads, 32 MB of L3 cache, and lacks local storage or GPU accelerators. Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core CPU execution, but weak multi-core scaling and poor memory bandwidth, with large-block read speeds of 26.64 GB/sec. This instance is a cost-effective choice for lightweight, single-threaded tasks, basic text processing, and low-traffic web serving, but it is not recommended for database operations or multi-threaded compilation due to resource constraints.
